title: Could Auto Executives Make President Trump End the Trade War?
text: Could Auto Executives Make President Trump End the Trade War? More Could Auto Executives Make President Trump End the Trade War?## The auto industryLast week, the S&P 500 Index (SPY), NASDAQ Composite Index, and Dow Jones inched up 2.5%, 3.5%, and 2.4%, respectively. The broader market started the third week of January on a slightly negative note. Today at 2:42 PM ET, the S&P 500 Index was down 0.5%. In the last few months, factors such as rising interest rates, the US–China trade war, and fears of a global economic slowdown have taken a toll on investor sentiment. The US automobile industry has been one of the worst-affected sectors in terms of the US–China trade tensions.## Auto executives’ message to TrumpAccording to a Reuters report, senior auto executives urged President Trump “and Congress to resolve trade disputes, and end the government shutdown, saying political uncertainty is costing the industry.”The report explained that Fiat Chrysler Automobiles’ (FCAU) CEO, Mike Manley, expects US tariffs on steel and aluminum to “raise the automaker’s 2019 costs by $300 million to $350 million, or about $135 to $160 a vehicle, based on the automaker’s 2018 U.S. sales.”The report quoted General Motors’ (GM) president, Mark Reuss, saying, “Those are headwinds, It’s our job to run the business to offset those headwinds.”## Will Trump listen?In the last couple of quarters, automakers (XLY) including General Motors, Ford, and Tesla (TSLA) have warned investors of the negative impact of the US–China trade tensions (FXI) on their earnings and profitability. The trade war has made it increasingly difficult for US companies to compete with local Chinese peers.Not only automakers but also many other tech companies—including Apple (AAPL) and Starbucks (SBUX)—are facing the heat of the US–China trade tensions. Earlier this month, AAPL cut its guidance for the last quarter, mainly due to its slowing Chinese sales.It will be interesting to see how Trump reacts—if he does react—to auto executives’ request to end the trade war.
